title: Water and suggestive selling
lead: Water first, with no surprises on the check. Then suggestions that are simply help.

sections.name: Water service
know: No surprises be clear about any charge.
Still or sparkling offer both, so guests choose freely.
One third full: that’s when you refill.

rows.name: House still
rows.meta: Our everyday pour. Offer it to every table.

rows.name: House sparkling
rows.meta: Offer it alongside still, so guests can choose freely.

rows.name: Bottled waters
rows.meta: Any your restaurant sells: present the label to the host, open and pour tableside. Say if there’s a charge.

sections.name: Suggestive selling

lines.label: In short
lines.text: A great suggestion is simply help.

know: Help that’s all a great suggestion is.
Ask first light or rich, adventurous or classic?
Two, not ten a favorite, in sensory words.
Pairings each suggestion completes the one before.

keyPoints.line: offer both, so guests choose freely.

read.where: Offer **water first, before anything else**: house still and sparkling, plus any **bottled waters** your restaurant sells. Always be **clear about any charge** so there are **no surprises on the check**.

stops.name: Hold the glass by the base
Refill at one third
stops.text: Refill when a glass is **about one third full**, so **no glass is ever empty**.

read.sayIt: May I offer you still or sparkling water?

keyPoints.line: that’s all a great suggestion is.
light or rich, adventurous or classic?
each suggestion completes the one before.

read.bigIdea: A great suggestion is simply help.
read.where: Guiding the guest toward the **best possible meal**. **Revenue follows naturally from trust.**

stops.name: Ask first, then suggest
stops.text: Learn what they **lean toward** (light or rich, adventurous or classic) before you recommend.

stops.name: Offer two, not ten
stops.text: Share a **personal favorite** and describe it in **sensory words**; a short, confident answer beats a long list.

stops.name: Think in pairings
stops.text: Connect **cocktails, wine, courses and dessert** so each suggestion completes the one before it.

stops.name: Read the table
stops.text: Celebrations welcome a **toast**; a quiet dinner may want a **lighter touch**. **Never pressure**, and honor every “no” graciously.

read.sayIt: The [starter] is what I’d begin with tonight. It sets up the [main] beautifully, and a glass of the [wine] is lovely alongside both.

sources: The Art of Table Service: 9, Water Service, and 10, Suggestive Selling.
